主要内容: The Consumer Price Index (CPI) for All Urban Consumers declined by 0.1 percent from January 2014 to January 2015, marking the first over-the-year decline since the 12-month period ending October 2009. This decline was primarily driven by a significant drop in energy prices, with the energy index falling 19.6 percent. The gasoline index dropped 35.4 percent, and the fuel oil index fell 29.7 percent. Electricity was the only major energy item to rise, increasing by 2.5 percent. The food index rose 3.2 percent, with prices for food at home increasing 3.3 percent and prices for food away from home rising 3.1 percent. The index for all items less food and energy rose 1.6 percent, the same as for the period ended December 2014. The shelter index increased by 2.9 percent. These data are from the Consumer Price Index program and are not seasonally adjusted.
